content.title: Chwalinska edges Sakkari in Wuhan thriller to make third WTA semifinal
content.description: Maja Chwalinska showed both creativity and grit to defeat Maria Sakkari in the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open quarterfinals advancing to her third career tour-level semifinal, second of the Asian Swing and first on outdoor hard courts.
content.body:
Roland Garros finalist Maja Chwalinska will make her Top 20 debut on Monday after the No. 16 seed edged Maria Sakkari 6-0, 3-6, 7-5 in a 2-hour, 35-minute barnburner on Friday to make the final four at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open.

It will be the third tour-level semifinal, and first on outdoor hard courts, of Chwalinska's career. Two of those semifinals have come in the past month, following her run to the last four in Singapore. The Pole has used her Asian Swing debut to demonstrate that the creative game style that enthralled fans during her Parisian breakthrough can be just as effective away from clay. So far on the continent, she's compiled a 7-2 record, including her first pair of Top 20 wins.

Chwalinska to face Swiatek for first time 10 years

Chwalinska will get the chance to extend that further when she takes on childhood friend, former junior doubles partner and Polish compatriot Iga Swiatek in the semifinals. It will mark the first time that two Poles have faced each other in the semifinals of a WTA 1000 event.

"I feel like I know her forever," Chwalinska said. "Because basically we started playing tournaments together. It would be amazing, really. I think it would be great for us, and great for Polish tennis as well. It would be a great honor for me also, because she's such a great champion. She's done almost everything in our sport, so it would be a great privilege to play."

Together, Chwalinska and Swiatek won European Junior Championships doubles crowns at both U14 level (in 2015) and U16 level (2016), and were the 2017 Australian Open girls' doubles runners-up to Bianca Andreescu and Carson Branstine.

Against each other, they first played in 2014 at a U14 event in Opalenica, Poland, with eventual champion Swiatek winning 6-1, 6-4 in the quarterfinals. Their only professional meeting came two years later, in the second round of the 2016 Stockholm W10 -- Swiatek's second ever pro tournament. She was the winner again, 6-2, 6-3, but fell in the next round to Kristina Schmiedlova.

Familiar foe Sakkari brought familiar fight to Chwalinska

In the previous round, Chwalinska had dismantled 18-year-old Iva Jovic's game, delivering a masterclass in variety to win nine of the last 10 games. She picked up where she left off against Sakkari, skilfully out-manoeuvring the Greek player and dropping just one point behind her first serve. The left-handed Chwalinska even pulled off a remarkable right-handed lob, stretched far out wide by Sakkari's hefty attempted one-two punch.

Having to use her non-dominant arm didn't hamper Chwalinska's touch in the slightest: the lob was pinpoint perfect, and an effective reset of a rally she ultimately claimed with a succession of backhand winners.

The 25-year-old sealed her fifth career 6-0 set at tour level with a terrific angled pass, and held a break point in the first game of the second set -- only to send a too-cute backhand slice just wide. That was the cue for Sakkari, who had contributed 14 unforced errors in a wayward first set, to raise her level and rein her game in.

The former No. 3 struck in the very next game, putting away a forehand winner to break for the first time -- a lead she held on to throughout an impressive second set, in which she fired 17 winners to only eight unforced errors.

In the opener, Sakkari had been drawn into error by Chwalinska's variety and placement; now, she was able to stick in extended rallies, and answer Chwalinska's most creative plays with even superior ones. Twice in the fourth game, Chwalinska attempted to foil Sakkari with defensive drop shots; both times, Sakkari not only reached them but had the wherewithal to steer sliced backhand winners into the corner.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

The stage was set for a riveting decider in which both players held firm on serve through the first 11 games. Sakkari repeatedly showed her mettle when facing break points, frequently finding her best forehands and volleys to fend them off -- but she also found herself under that pressure more often than Chwalinska. The 31-year-old saved the first five break points against her in the third set (across three separate games) -- indeed, she saved 11 out of 15 during the whole match.

Chwalinska, though, had a similarly impressive rate of saving break points -- while having to face far fewer. She staved off four out of five overall, including the only one against her in the third set (with a drive volley winner in the fifth game). Repeatedly, Chwalinska was able to reset after missing opportunities on Sakkari's serve with a relatively straightforward hold.

"I was surprised about this number," Chwalinska said when asked about those break point statistics. "I didn't think about that. But I felt like in the third set, I was very solid on my serve and had a few chances on her service games -- but I mean, during the break points I think she covered them really well and honestly I couldn't do much. So I feel like I was just very solid during my service games today."

The World No. 22 had also adjusted her tactics as Sakkari had cut down her mistakes. She used her drop shot-lob combination more frequently in the decider than in the previous two sets, wheeling it out four times in one mid-set five-game stretch and winning the point every time.

In the final game of the match, Chwalinska deployed that pattern yet again to get herself into another Sakkari service game. Having worked so hard to keep her accuracy disciplined for nearly two sets, Sakkari then reverted to her first-set form in the home stretch, netting a forehand on her own game point then a short backhand down a first match point.

Despite cruising to the first set, the way in which the match played out was no surprise to Chwalinska. Having lost to Sakkari in their first meeting in 2025 Rome qualifying, she had won their third-round rematch at Roland Garros 1-6, 6-3, 6-2 -- but that had been the only set she had conceded before the final.

"It was such a physical match," she said. "Of course, I expected a very tough match against Maria. I played her twice already and both the occasions were very, very tough. It wasn't different today."

content.title: Kartal’s comeback gathers pace with landmark run to Wuhan semifinals
content.description: After six months out with a back injury, Britain’s Sonay Kartal has surged into her first WTA 1000 semifinal, upsetting world No. 6 Elina Svitolina in Wuhan. She will face former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko next, with both players now one victory away from reaching their first WTA 1000 final.

content.body:
After six months on the sidelines with a back injury that saw her ranking tumble from No. 54 to No. 170, Britain’s Sonay Kartal might have hoped to find some rhythm during her comeback, which began last month.

Instead, the 24-year-old finds herself in the semifinals of a WTA 1000 tournament for the first time after knocking out world No. 6 Elina Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 in the quarterfinals of the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open on Friday. 

After the players split the first two sets, each winning 6-2, the third set went down to the wire. Both held serve through the first nine games, with neither facing a break point until the 10th. Kartal then earned her first break point of the set -- which was also a match point -- and converted it to seal a 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 victory in 2 hours, 3 minutes.

The victory over Svitolina was Kartal's first against the Ukrainian in three meetings. It also extended her unbeaten record to 12-0 in 2026 in WTA-level main draws when she wins the first set. 

"I'm very proud to get through that one," she said in her post-match press conference. "It was far from easy. I played at the very start of the year in Auckland. I know her pretty well, so I know that until the last point was played, I was never safe. I'm proud of the level that I managed to produce. And I'm very happy that I've been so consistent this week."

It was Kartal’s second career win over a top-10 opponent and sent her into just her second career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz semifinal. At No. 170, she also became the third-lowest-ranked semifinalist at a WTA 1000 event since the format was introduced in 2009, behind only Sloane Stephens (Toronto 2017, No. 934) and Victoria Azarenka (Miami 2018, No. 186),

The story continues 🔥 Sonay Kartal defeats Svitolina 6-2, 2-6, 6-4 to move into the semifinals in Wuhan! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/T9V3cl0ROk

— wta (@WTA) October 16, 2026
"I think I'm just growing in confidence with every match that I'm playing"

Since returning to competition last month, Kartal has represented Great Britain in the Billie Jean King Cup and reached the third round in Beijing, where she defeated world No. 31 Wang Xinyu. She has continued that momentum in Wuhan, recording wins over world No. 48 Anhelina Kalinina, No. 9 seed Belinda Bencic and No. 15 seed Jasmine Paolini before overcoming Svitolina.

"I definitely did not think that I would find this level this fast," she said. "I think it's a bit of a surprise to me. I've had my best wins in my third tournament back. I did lose six months on the tour, but I don't feel like that when I'm playing on the court. So, for me, that's a big positive.

"I think now that I'm back, I'm just going to try and maintain this level and try and find my ceiling and see where I can get to in the next year or so."

"The biggest advice I received was don't rush it"

Kartal revealed that she had actually been ready to return in late August but chose to listen to the advice of those around her rather than rush her recovery.

“I was ready to get back kind of end of August time but I knew I was going to come back to these events," she added. "I had to try and replicate the environment of a match as best as you can in training. I don't think you can replicate it, but I didn't rush myself.

“I've got a lot of tennis years left in me, so I took advice from a lot of other players who have had lengthy injuries. I just had a great physio down here and I just trusted in her and trusted in the team that when I would get back. I didn't know that I would get back to the level that I know I can do.”

The decision to be patient was not an easy one. Kartal acknowledged the the disappointment of missing some of the sport's biggest events, including her home Slam at Wimbledon, but said she had learned to trust her support team.

“I think the biggest advice I received was don't rush it," she said. "When you're playing an individual sport, you want to get back as quickly as you can for many reasons, financially and, I love playing in these atmospheres... but I had to trust the people around me. I know I have the best in the game and at the end of the day, they know what they're doing.

"I might be stubborn and want to try and push them, but ultimately I've got to sit back and listen. It's rare as a tennis player you get six months away, so I tried to make the most of it.”

Ostapenko awaits in the semifinals

Kartal will next face former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko in Saturday's semifinals, with the pair tied 1-1 in their career meetings. Kartal won their encounter at Wimbledon in 2025, while Ostapenko prevailed at Eastbourne the same year.

"She hits a great big ball on a grass court so I'm hoping this court can slow down a little bit for me, but again, I know I'm in for a good battle," Kartal said looking ahead to the semifinal. She's been playing great this week. Once again, it's going to be another tough battle.

Ostapenko booked her place in the last four with a 7-5, 6-1 victory over No. 11 seed Diana Shnaider in the first quarterfinal of the day.

OUTSTANDING OSTAPENKO ⭐️ @JelenaOstapenk8 defeats Shnaider in straight sets and advances into the semifinals! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/DYWpUwFFmN

— wta (@WTA) October 16, 2026

"It was a great match,” Ostapenko said after her win. “I was down in the first set, but then I was fighting and found a way in the first set and then I think I played a really good second set."

Ostapenko is through to the Wuhan semifinals for the second time in her career, nine years after losing to Ash Barty at the same stage in 2017. She will be aiming to reach her fourth WTA 1000 final and win her first title at that level.

“I have great memories from Wuhan achieving semi-finals here and I remember I beat World No. 1 on the Center Court so I have great memories and also with the Chinese fans always like it's great to be here and to have a lot of support.”

She will face former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko next, with both players now one victory away from reaching their first WTA 1000 final.

content.description: The BNB Ningbo Open serves as the second-to-last WTA 500 event of the season, and is currently headlined by Elena Rybakina, Elina Svitolina, Iga Swiatek and more. Here is everything you need to know.

content.body:
Following the final WTA 1000 event of the season in Wuhan, the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz continues with the BNB Ningbo Open. 

Ningbo plays host to the penultimate WTA 500 event of the season, and 2026 marks its third edition of a tournament at the level. Defending champion and World No. 1 Elena Rybakina headlines the field as she builds up to the 2026 WTA Finals at Indian Wells. 

Here's everything to know about this year's Ningbo Open:

What are the dates for each round?

Main draw play from Ningbo begins Monday, October 19, and ends with the championships on Sunday, October 25. The doubles final will be held at 2:30 p.m. local time, with the singles final to follow, not before 5 p.m.

Time conversions: 5 p.m. China Standard Time = 5 a.m. Eastern Time, 9 a.m. Greenwich Mean Time

Singles

First round: October 19-20
Second round: October 21-22
Quarterfinals: October 23
Semifinals: October 24
Final: October 25

Doubles

First round: October 29-21
Quarterfinals: October 22-22
Semifinals: October 24
Final: October 25

How big is the draw, and who are the top players in the field?

Ningbo will feature a 28-player singles draw and 16-team doubles draw. The top four singles players at the time of seeding will receive byes into the second round. 

Projected seeded players

  1. Elena Rybakina
  2. Elina Svitolina
  3. Iga Swiatek
  4. Marta Kostyuk
  5. Iva Jovic
  6. Belinda Bencic

Remaining direct entrants: Sorana Cirstea, Alexandra Eala, Maja Chwalinska, Ekaterina Alexandrova, Marie Bouzkova, Sara Bejlek, Jasmine Paolini

Wild cards: To be determined

Withdrawals: Anna Kalinskaya (illness), Jessica Pegula 

Moved into main draw: Diane Parry, Leylah Fernandez

Player list is subject to change

Draw: The main draw will be determined at 7 p.m. local time on Saturday, October 17. 

Who are the defending champions?

Rybakina won her 10th career singles title in Ningbo last season, defeating Alexandrova 3-6, 6-0, 6-2.

At the time, she entered the tournament ranked No. 9, but her run in Ningbo was the foundation for her 2025 WTA Finals Riyadh title and a 2026 season that saw her win two more Grand Slam titles and take the No. 1 ranking. 

In addition to Alexandrova, she also defeated Dayana Yastremska, Ajla Tomljanovic and Jasmine Paolini, the initial four wins of a 11-match winning streak to end her 2025 season. 

In doubles, Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Liudmila Samsonova defeated Timea Babos and Luisa Stefani 5-7, 6-4, [10-8]. 

What are the prize money and ranking points at stake?

The tournament will have a collective prize pool of approximately $1,206,446. As with all WTA 500 events, a maximum of 500 ranking points are available depending on how far a player or team advances in the tournament.

content.title: Zheng Qinwen to miss Japan Open with continued shoulder injury
content.description: Zheng Qinwen will miss next week's Kinoshita Group Japan Open in Osaka, citing a continued shoulder injury. It's her second consecutive withdrawal following her milestone title in Beijing.

content.body:
Zheng Qinwen will miss next week's WTA 250 Kinoshita Group Japan Open in Osaka, citing a continued shoulder injury.

It's the second consecutive withdrawal for Zheng, after pulling out of Wuhan earlier this week. 

Zheng's withdrawals come on the heels of her milestone title in Beijing, where she became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open. In the main draw as a wild card, she won four consecutive three-setters before upsetting Elina Svitolina in the quarterfinals, Elise Mertens in the semifinals and Mirra Andreeva in the final. 

She spent 15 hours and 16 minutes on court during her seven matches in Beijing. That's the most time spent on court by any player at any tournament this year, and the most since Opta began tracking total time spent on court in 2023. 

It was Zheng's first career WTA 1000 title, and her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title since 2024.

"Since returning from injury, I have played a demanding stretch of tennis over the past month and a half, competing at the US Open, the Billie Jean King Cup and the China Open," Zheng said in a statement after withdrawing from Wuhan. "My body is feeling very fatigued after this intense run of matches."

Since the start of the US Open, where Zheng reached the quarterfinals as a qualifier, she has won 14 of her last 15 matches, with the lone loss coming to World No. 1 Elena Rybakina. Nine of those 15 matches went to three sets.

Zheng came into the US Open ranked No. 121 in the PIF WTA Rankings, and in less than two months she's risen 98 spots, to No. 23.

World No. 68 Ashlyn Krueger has moved into the main draw in Zheng's absence.

Zheng is still scheduled to play the WTA 250 Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open next month, one of the final two tournaments on the calendar before the WTA Finals at Indian Wells.

The Kinoshita Group Japan Open will begin on Oct. 19 and run through Oct. 25.

content.title: By the numbers: Swiatek's 150th WTA 1000 win boosts WTA Finals chances
content.description: Iga Swiatek notched her 150th WTA 1000 win Thursday night in Wuhan, defeating lucky loser Ashlyn Krueger 6-1, 6-4 to reach the quarterfinals for the second straight year. The win also strengthened her bid for a WTA Finals berth.

related.label: Career-best win sends Chwalinska into the Wuhan Open quarterfinals

content.body:
Iga Swiatek collected her 150th WTA 1000 win Thursday night in Wuhan, defeating lucky loser Ashlyn Krueger 6-1, 6-4 in 1 hour, 34 minutes to reach the quarterfinals for the second consecutive year.

Wuhan: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Among the seven players to reach the milestone since the format's introduction in 2009, Swiatek (187) did so in the fewest matches. Since 1990, she is just the third player to record at least 150 wins within her first 50 Tier I or WTA 1000 main draws, joining Martina Hingis (162) and Serena Williams (153).

The milestone also helped Swiatek gain ground in the race to qualify for the WTA Finals Indian Wells. Karolina Muchova, who currently occupies the final qualification spot, fell to Diana Shnaider earlier Thursday in the Round of 16.

"It's not easy at the end of the season, so I'm really focusing on recovering every day as much as possible," Swiatek said in her on-court interview. "But I'm happy to get some wins, because I feel like I'm playing better than at the beginning of the season, so I'm ready to push and happy to be in the quarters."

Swiatek has now reached seven WTA 1000 quarterfinals in 2026, surpassing Elena Rybakina for the most by any player this season. It marked her 32nd career WTA 1000 quarterfinal. Only Aryna Sabalenka (33) has reached more among active players.

It wasn't Swiatek's sharpest performance, but her steadiness under pressure, combined with Krueger's mounting error count, carried her to a relatively straightforward victory.

Soaring into the quarterfinals 🪽 @iga_swiatek moves past Krueger in straight sets! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/ag2ysyCRAQ

— wta (@WTA) October 15, 2026

Here are the key numbers from Swiatek's latest victory and what they could mean for the former World No. 1 moving forward:

5: Consecutive WTA Finals appearances. The 2023 champion has qualified for the year-end championships every year since making her debut in 2021. Entering the week, she was tracking toward an alternate position, but a few more wins could further tighten the race.

7: Break points saved. Swiatek excelled in the biggest moments on serve, saving seven of eight break points. Krueger created opportunities throughout the match, but Swiatek consistently came up with timely responses to escape trouble.

9: Wins against lucky losers. As a result, Swiatek improved to 9-0 against lucky losers in her career, with eight of those victories coming in straight sets. Her only three-set win over a lucky loser came against Zheng Qinwen in San Diego in 2022.

41: WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz match wins in 2026. With two more wins in Wuhan, Swiatek has improved to 41 victories on this season. She has been particularly effective since the return to hard courts, posting an 18-3 record since Toronto.

46: Unforced errors by Krueger. The American generated more winners than Swiatek (16-9) but undermined her efforts with 46 unforced errors, 19 more than her opponent. Many of her best opportunities disappeared through self-inflicted mistakes.

Swiatek will face Ann Li, who upset top seed Aryna Sabalenka in the second round Wednesday, in the quarterfinals. Swiatek lost her only previous meeting with Li via retirement in Madrid earlier this season.

content.title: Breaking down the quarterfinal matchups in Wuhan
content.description: We're down to the final eight in Wuhan. Ann Li plays Iga Swiatek, Maja Chwalinska takes on Maria Sakkari, Elina Svitolina faces Sonay Kartal and Diana Shnaider plays Jelena Ostapenko. We break down the quarterfinal matchups.

related.label: Zheng Qinwen to miss Japan Open with continued shoulder injury
Career-best win sends Chwalinska into the Wuhan Open quarterfinals

content.body:
This time last week, only one top-five seed remained in the hunt in the Beijing quarterfinals.

The same is true this week in Wuhan, where World No. 5 Elina Svitolina is the highest-seeded player left in the field.

Unseeded Zheng Qinwen took advantage of the opportunity in Beijing, and Ann Li, Maria Sakkari, Sonay Kartal and Jelena Ostapenko will look to follow in her footsteps in the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season.

Here's everything you need to know about the quarterfinal matchups in Wuhan.

Ann Li vs. [7] Iga Swiatek

Li leads the head-to-head 1-0

Li is still riding high after upsetting World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka, the biggest win of her career. The 26-year-old American showed tremendous poise and resilience in that match, converting her 10th match point in an epic 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) win. 

"I think on some of those match points I was about to lose my mind," she said after the match. "I was about to crash out."

Instead, she stayed within herself, trusted her shots and persevered. And despite all the whirlwind of emotions that accompanied that match, there was no post-Sabalenka hangover. Li took care of business again on Thursday, beating Janice Tjen in straight sets, and she's into her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Swiatek, by contrast, is into her 32nd WTA 1000 quarterfinal, including seven this year. And every match from here on out carries significant weight. Not only is she playing for the Wuhan title, but she remains in contention for a WTA Finals berth. Swiatek has yet to drop a set through two matches, and she looked particularly strong on her return on Thursday, saving seven of eight break points against Ashlyn Krueger.

In their lone match on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, earlier this year in Madrid, Swiatek retired with a gastrointestinal illness while trailing 3-0 in the third set.

[16] Maja Chwalinska vs. Maria Sakkari

Head-to-head tied at 1-1

It's been a welcome return to Wuhan for Sakkari, who last played this tournament in 2018. She's had success here before, making the semifinals in 2017, and she has an opportunity to match that result on Friday. Sakkari had one of her wins of the season in the second round, a come-from-behind upset of Marta Kostyuk, sandwiched between two straight-set wins over Donna Vekic and 17-year-old wild card Mia Pohankova. 

She'll play Chwalinska, who is having the best tournament of her career outside of her breakthrough run to the Roland Garros final. Chwalinska recovered from 6-1 down to beat Marie Bouzkova, then upset Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1, the biggest win of her career by ranking. Chwalinska was far more consistent than the American in that match, hitting 16 fewer unforced errors.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Sakkari came from a set down to beat Chwalinska in their first career meeting, last year in Rome. Chwalinska flipped the script at Roland Garros this year, winning 1-6, 6-3, 6-2. That match is still fresh in Chwalinska's memory.

"It was an extremely hard match," she told reporters in Wuhan. "I remember that I was struggling physically. It was very hot, and Maria played amazing in the first set. I remember that. I didn't basically have any chance. So I'm expecting a very tough match again."

[5] Elina Svitolina vs. Sonay Kartal

Svitolina leads the head-to-head 2-0

Similar to Sakkari, this is Svitolina's first time in Wuhan in quite awhile. Prior to this week, she had last played this tournament in 2019, when she made the quarterfinals. She's back there again after a pair of wins over Liudmila Samsonova and Chinese wild card Guo Hanyu, the latter of whom had spent nearly six hours on court going into their match. Svitolina, who is inching her way towards a WTA Finals berth, wasn't at her best against Guo despite the 6-1, 6-4 scoreline. She made less than 50 percent of her first serves and made 32 unforced errors, though she did create 16 break points, converting seven of them.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Kartal, on the other hand, was locked in from start to finish in her third-round win over Jasmine Paolini, a clinical 6-2, 6-0 beating that took just 67 minutes. She had 14 winners to just eight unforced errors, and won the last 11 games. Playing just her third tournament following a sixth-month injury layoff, she's yet to drop a set in three matches, including another upset of ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic.

Svitolina and Kartal played at the very start of the year, in Auckland. It was a tight back-and-forth battle, with Svitolina narrowly winning 6-4, 6-7 (2), 7-6 (5).

[11] Diana Shnaider vs. Jelena Ostapenko

First career meeting

Coming into this tournament, Shnaider didn't have the fondest memories of Wuhan. She had played here twice, and lost in the first round each time. And after arriving from Beijing after reaching the doubles semifinals, she didn't have the highest hopes that this would be the year she'd turn it around.

"When I came here, I was dead mentally, and definitely wasn't expecting to do great," she said.

To her surprise, she has been great -- nearly flawless, in fact. Shnaider has won all three of her matches this week in straight sets, the last of which was a 7-5, 6-3 upset of sixth-seeded Karolina Muchova.

She'll face Ostapenko, who has had a far more laborious path to the quarterfinals. She dropped just two games in her first-round win over Daria Kasatkina, but from there she was pushed to her limit by second-seeded Jessica Pegula. After dropping the first set 6-2, she saved three match point in the second-set tiebreak in a thrilling 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-3 win. She went the distance again on Thursday, beating Leylah Fernandez 6-1, 1-6, 6-4.

content.body:
French Open runner-up and No. 16 seed Maja Chwalinska scored the biggest win of her career by ranking, upsetting world No. 11 Iva Jovic in straight sets 6-4, 6-1 to reach the quarterfinals at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open.

In a matchup between two of the season's breakout stars, Chwalinska earned the decisive break in the ninth game of the first set before holding serve to take it 6-4.

With the opening set under her belt, Chwalinska dominated the second as the errors mounted for the 10th seeded Jovic. After the pair traded holds to start the set, the Pole won five consecutive games to complete the victory in 1 hour and 49 minutes.

— wta (@WTA) October 15, 2026

Chwalinska was the more consistent player on the day, hitting 17 winners against 15 unforced errors. Jovic struck 23 winners but committed 31 unforced errors.

"I think it was quite a solid match from my side," Chwalinska said in her post-match press conference. "Iva is an amazing player. I knew that I needed to play my best game to get a win today.

"I think we had many very challenging rallies and it was a very physical match, I think, even though the score maybe doesn't show it, but it was definitely a very hard match. Yeah, very happy about the performance."

'Definitely a moment to appreciate for sure'

Reaching the last eight in Wuhan is another milestone for Chwalinska in what has been her most successful season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz so far, something which she acknowledges and appreciates.

"It has been a great year for me for sure," Chwalinska told the media. "Very unforgettable year. Last year I was in a different position for sure. I was probably preparing for South American clay courts tournaments at the end of the year and now here I am, so very happy, very grateful for that.

"Actually, I talked with my physio today, who is also the physio of our Billie Jean King Cup team. And we talked, I think, in April when we had a tie in Poland. I was maybe 120 [in the rankings]. You know, I'm just not feeling like I fulfilled my potential and I'm getting old. And he's here with me now, and I'm probably going to be top 20. So, it's definitely a moment to appreciate for sure."

She'll next face Maria Sakkari in the last eight. The Greek defeated wild card Mia Pohankova 6-1, 6-4 in another third-round match Thursday.

This will be the third career meeting between the two players. Sakkari won the pair's first meeting in the qualifying rounds in Rome last year, prevailing in three sets. Chwalinska gained revenge with a three-set victory over Sakkari n the third round of the French Open this year.

content.body:
WUHAN -- The past two years at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open, Diana Shnaider's stay was short. 

She hadn't won one match in Wuhan -- both singles and doubles -- until this year's edition. With a 7-5, 6-3 win Karolina Muchova, Shnaider is through to the quarterfinals. She picked up her fourth top 10 win of her career -- three this season -- and she's into her fourth career WTA 1000 quarterfinal. All of her wins at the tournament thus far have come in straight sets.

It's been a strong year for the World No. 13, who's amassed a 32-20 record on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in 2026. Her season has been highlighted by a semifinal runs at Roland Garros, Adelaide and Washington, and quarterfinal finishes in Toronto and Charleston, and she's maintaining the consistency into the Asian Swing. 

"It wasn't a lot of time to adjust to the new courts, new balls," Shnaider said on coming to Wuhan after reaching Beijing doubles semifinals. "It was a little bit hard just mentally that you had just one day where you can forget about tennis. And then all over again, but this is what happens when you go a little bit deeper in a tournament.

"I'm very happy that I'm in the quarters because when I just came here, I was dead mentally, and definitely wasn't expecting to do great."

Shnaider's been consistent over the last three seasons on tour, hovering in and out of the top 20. She achieved her career-high rank of No. 11 in May 2025, and she sits at No. 13 right now. Two years ago at Wuhan, she entered as No. 16 on tour. 

As her consistency has strengthened, Shnaider has also invested more into her team.

Her lead coach, Sascha Bajin, has been with her since August 2025, and now she travels more frequently with fitness coaches and rotating hitting partners. The concept of building a team has been a learning curve for Shnaider, but she's figured out the balance on what tournaments to bring a whole team vs. a reduced operation. She also has fitness coaches in select areas geographically depending where she is on tour, such as the United States.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

"It takes a little bit more time to create the team around you. You need to find the right people and obviously sometime it is hard," Shnaider said. "I'm just trying to figure out what type of mindset I want to have on tournaments, off the tournaments, because everyone wants to have a success.

"Everyone wants to help you, but sometimes you understand and maybe this one is a little bit too much, maybe this one is a little bit less. So I'm just trying to find myself what I want to have on tournaments, between tournaments, before matches to what's the most comfortable for me."

The first part of the 2025 season saw fluctuation in Shnaider's team, but by bringjing Bajin on board -- and his plethora of experience -- the consistency in her team itself has fueled the strong year. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

From both tactical and mental perspectives, Shnaider lauded the partnership. 

"We keep working on the court and a lot of different stuff, and I feel there is still a lot of things that we can do more and work more because work never stops. We also talk a lot about the tactics, the easier shot, the short placement and everything.

"We talk the mental side of it, like today. 'It's okay, if it's nine times deuce, but you got to go. If it's nine, it's nine. If it's five, it's five. If it's 15, 15. You're not going to let your emotions in front of you [or] get tired."

Shnaider could reach her fourth semifinal of the year, and faces the winner of Jelena Ostapenko and Leylah Fernandez in Friday's quarterfinals.

content.description: Ann Li let nine match points slip away, but she outlasted Aryna Sabalenka 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) in 2 hours and 27 minutes to earn the biggest win of her career. The victory was Li's first over Sabalenka and sent her into the Wuhan third round for the first time.

content.body:
Ann Li had to work for it, but she rallied from a set down and converted her 10th match point to upset No. 1 seed Aryna Sabalenka 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) in 2 hours and 27 minutes on Wednesday for the biggest win of her career.

Wuhan: Scores | Order of play | Draws

It marked Li's third career Top 10 win and second this season. It was also her career-best win by ranking and her first over Sabalenka in four WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz meetings. With the win, she advanced to the third round of a WTA 1000 event for the fourth consecutive time -- a personal best -- and reached that stage in Wuhan for the first time.

"I think on some of those match points I was about to lose my mind. I was about to crash out," Li said in her post-match press conference. "In the end, you just have to realize -- I didn't even play that bad. I didn't play bad. She just played really well. So you have to play point by point. And I knew that if I stayed there, I could get into that situation again, which is all you can ask for."

THE BIGGEST WIN OF HER CAREER 💪 Ann Li defeats the No.1 seed in Wuhan! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/UXmnwsiJDK

— wta (@WTA) October 14, 2026

Li dropped the opening set after Sabalenka won eight straight points to close it out and soon found herself down a break at 4-2 in the second. But she responded by winning nine of the next 11 games, forcing a decider and building a commanding 5-2 lead in the third.

What followed was a determined effort from Sabalenka, who received a visit from the physio midway through the final set to reapply tape to her right leg. She saved five match points to hold for 5-3, then erased two more at 5-4 with a forehand winner and a backhand winner to level at 5-5. A love hold two games later sent the match into a deciding tiebreak.

There, Sabalenka fought off two more match points, including one with a remarkable forehand that just caught the corner. But Li finally sealed the victory with a forehand winner on her 10th match point.

What it means

Li's victory over the three-time champion and four-time semifinalist means Sabalenka will fail to reach the last four in Wuhan for the first time. Instead, the American moves on to face Janice Tjen in the Round of 16. It will be their first career meeting. 

"I think we've practiced a few times," Li said. "She's a great player. She likes to [use] variety as well, so it should be a really fun match. Physical wise, I feel pretty good."

Both players will be aiming to reach their first WTA 1000 quarterfinal. Li has lost all three of her previous WTA 1000 Round of 16 appearances, though she has won eight of her past nine matches against lower-ranked opponents.

content.title: 'In the moment' Ostapenko saves three match points, stuns Pegula in Wuhan
content.description: Jelena Ostapenko saved three match points in the second-set tiebreak to upset Jessica Pegula in the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open second round.

related.label: Around Wuhan: Muchova's impressive tiebreak feat; Jovic, Chwalinska set to meet
'It feels like it was a century ago': Sakkari recounts 2017 Wuhan breakthrough
By the numbers: Gauff and Pegula are making WTA Finals history one year at a time

content.body:
Jelena Ostapenko pulled off a thrilling turnaround in the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open second round, saving three match points in the second-set tiebreak to upset No. 2 seed and 2025 runner-up Jessica Pegula 2-6, 7-6(7), 6-3 in 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The result is Ostapenko's third Top 10 win of 2026, and 28th of her career -- and the first time she has beaten a Top 5 opponent since last year's Stuttgart final, where she defeated Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 6-1. It's the third time that she's defeated Pegula in seven meetings dating back to 2015, following her 3-6, 6-2, 7-6(3) win in the 2015 Québec City second round and her 6-4, 6-2 win in the Beijing second round. It's also a revenge of sorts for her 2023 Doha loss, in which Pegula saved two match points for a 6-2, 2-6, 7-5 victory.

Ostapenko will next face either Leylah Fernandez or qualifier Shi Han as she bids to reach her third WTA 1000 quarterfinal of the season.

How did Ostapenko pull off the comeback?

As is often the case with Ostapenko, her ratio of winners to unforced errors can fluctuate from one extreme to the other with little warning. In the first set, she was barely able to stay in longer exchanges, winning just two points when the rally exceeded four shots and committing 11 unforced errors.

The 2017 Roland Garros champion's form ticked up slightly at the setart of the second set, but Pegula kept her foot on the pedal to break for 3-2. Ostapenko received a medical timeout at this juncture and returned to court with her right arm heavily strapped.

"I had a lot of pain in my arm, then I took a painkiller and then I was fighting for every single point," she explained in her on-court interview.

Her form continued to improve as the set drew on -- but even so, Pegula's strategy of giving nothing away enabled her to advance to three match points in the tiebreak. On the first, with the court wide open, the American netted a simple volley. Ostapenko found a service winner on her second serve to save the second, then came up with an audacious drop shot play to save the third.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Surging with confidence, Ostapenko roared through the decider with a scintillating display of her customary power tennis, finishing the match with 46 winners (including 10 aces) to 37 unforced errors (including 11 double faults). Her return of serve was particularly breathtaking -- even when Ostapenko failed to convert a 30-0 lead when serving for the win, she simply recovered to break Pegula in the next game courtesy of two clean return winners.

It wasn't just Ostapenko's first strike that improved as the match went on, though. The Latvian won 23 rallies that went over four shots in the last two sets, including five that went over nine shots.

"The US swing was pretty bad for me," Ostapenko said in her press conference (she went 0-3 in it). "After that, I feel like I was practising well at home. I feel I'm in the right zone now and I feel like I'm doing the right decisions. Sometimes when I have to go for the shots I'm going for it, sometimes -- even when I play very aggressive -- but today some points I was just trying to keep the ball in play and wait for the good ball to attack. I feel like I was doing this really good today, and yesterday, and also in Beijing."

Anatomy of a hot shot: that drop shot down match point

The tried and trusted Ostapenko approach to tennis is to go with power at all times, and then with more power if necessary. Which is what makes her third match point save such a wild decision: after hammering the ball from side to side, unable to break through Pegula's defenses, Ostapenko attempted a drop shot for the first and only time in the match. It landed perfectly for a winner, curving away from Pegula and cut too fine for even her wheels to reach.

What was she thinking? Asked about it afterwards, Ostapenko's grin indicated she knew how unexpected a shot choice it had been.

"Honestly I don't even want to think what I was thinking, because I think I was not thinking anything," she said. "I was just in the moment. I think I play the best when I go by my -- it's funny to say, but with my instincts, with my feelings. I think you don't really have to think what you are doing. Just be in the moment and play tennis."

How many times has Ostapenko won from match point down?

This result is the seventh time that Ostapenko has won from match point down in a WTA main draw, and tied for the most match points she has saved en route to victory:

2016 Cincinnati R1, d. Anna Karolina Schmiedlova 1-6, 7-6(6), 7-6(5) -- saved two
2017 Prague R2, d. Caroline Wozniacki 5-7, 6-3, 7-6(5) -- saved one
2019 Charleston R2, d. Shelby Rogers 4-6, 6-3, 7-6(4) -- saved one
2019 Linz SF, d. Ekaterina Alexandrova 1-6, 7-6(5), 7-5 -- saved three
2022 Seoul R2, d. Anastasia Gasanova 6-3, 5-7, 7-5 -- saved one
2024 Linz R2, d. Clara Tauson 3-6, 6-4, 7-6(7) -- saved one
2026 Wuhan R2, d. Jessica Pegula 2-6, 7-6(7), 6-3 -- saved three

content.title: Around Wuhan: Muchova's impressive tiebreak feat; Jovic, Chwalinska set to meet
content.description: Around the grounds in Wuhan, Karolina Muchova maintained her perfect 10-0 tiebreak record to the season in a gritty comeback win over Caty McNally. Maja Chwalinska also came back, but in contrasting fashion, and is set to meet Iva Jovic in the third round.

content.body:
WUHAN -- No. 6 seed Karolina Muchova and No. 16 seed Maja Chwalinska both needed to win in comeback fashion in their Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open second-round matches Wednesday, but the two could not be more different. 

For Muchova, she went toe-to-toe with qualifier Caty McNally, who was seeking her third career top 10 win on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. McNally dominated the first set, and the match went down to the wire in the second and third sets, both requiring a tiebreak -- a situation that Muchova has thrived in this season.

The Czech is 10-0 in tiebreaks this season, becoming the first player this century to win their first 10 tiebreaks in a single season. Sanchez Vicario (2000) and Maria Sakkari (2020) both won their first nine.

Two of Muchova's 10 came in her 3-6, 7-6(1), 7-6(4) win over McNally. Last week in Beijing, she also won two more sets in tiebreaks, once in her opening match vs. Katie Boulter and the other against Naomi Osaka in a fourth-round match that saw her need nine match points to win. 

"I actually knew that this year I'm doing pretty great in tiebreaks," Muchova said to press. "In my head, I try to tell myself, 'Okay, it's tiebreak, it's my thing.' Kind of give myself confidence and try to play aggressive in my game from the start of both of the tiebreaks, and I think it is just paying off.

"Obviously, you never know in a breaker, and I think I catch the start of it and hit some good shots, winners, good serves. When you're a bit ahead in a tiebreak, you play until seven points so then I just felt closer and was more confident."

The victory also marked Muchova's 14th three-set win in 2026, the most she's had in a single season. She also has recorded eight come back wins, too, more than the last two years combined.

While Muchova recognizes that she's played significantly more matches this season compared to years past, she also attributed the reasoning to her grit on court. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

"I just obviously try to fight in every match and not just leave it there," Muchova said. "Today, I didn't feel so great in the first set. I wasn't feeling myself. And I think in the second set, when I broke her serve, I kind of like switched and I locked myself in a bubble and was swinging more freely.

"I just wanted to basically, not leave it there, just fight and try to get that win. That's what I try to do in every match. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't, but I'm glad that this year I have more numbers that did work."

Muchova is set to face [11] Diana Shnaider to begin play on Center Court Thursday. 

Chwalinska wins 12 of last 14 games vs. Bouzkova

Marie Bouzkova seemed to be well on her way to a spot in Wuhan's third round with a 6-1 first set against Chwalinska.

Then, the tables turned as Chwalinska each of the next two sets in a topsy-turvy 1-6, 6-1, 6-1 win. She's into her first Round of 16 at a WTA 1000 event, and will next face Iva Jovic. 

Jovic's path to the third round was much more streamlined in a 6-4, 6-1 win over Dayana Yastremska after a first-round bye. The 18-year-old American has seen the rise of Chwalinska ever since the Pole's breakthrough at Roland Garros. 

"She's had an incredible year and a big breakthrough," Jovic said. "Obviously, making finals of the Slam is a dream. I think it'll be a good match. She's definitely a crafty player. We've only practiced together once or twice, maybe, so it'll be interesting. We'll see who plays their game better."

No. 7 seed Iga Swiatek and No. 5 seed Elina Svitolina kept their bids for a spot at the WTA Finals alive with second-round wins at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open on Wednesday, albeit in contrasting fashion.

Swiatek had the easier path, scoring a 6-2, 6-1 win over fellow Polish player Magdalena Frech in 1 hour, 43 minutes. The victory was her 40th of the season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz and her 149th in WTA 1000 events, moving her past Serena Williams (148) into outright seventh place on the all-time list since the format's introduction in 2009.

"I'm happy to get the first match on the center court because I didn't get a chance to play there before," Swiatek told the media after her win. "At the beginning of the match, it was point by point, but then I was happy that I started making less mistakes and I used my chances till the end of the match. For sure it was tougher than the score."

Game, set, match 🎾 Iga Swiatek moves on into the last 16 in Wuhan, defeats Frech 6-2, 6-1. #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/kWig7Mk15e

— wta (@WTA) October 14, 2026

With her second win in as many meetings against the World No. 56, Swiatek improved to 19-2 against opponents ranked outside the top 50 this season. Her only two losses have come against No. 52 Maria Sakkari in Doha and No. 121 Zheng Qinwen at the US Open.

Swiatek describes 2026 season as her toughest

Swiatek has also recorded at least 40 wins in a season for the fifth consecutive year, a run of consistency she is pleased with.

"I mean every year has been so much different that there's no like recipe or solution," Swiatek said. "I'm happy that even though every year was different and presented different challenges, I'm able to be consistent and for sure this one has been.. toughest so still getting every win means a lot and you know I'll try to have as many as possible obviously."

Swiatek believes this season has been particularly challenging and she reflected on what she has learned from the struggles.

"Probably the biggest lesson will be that nothing will come easy because you know it kind of has been pretty up in my career going like always forward a little bit," she said. "When when I had some bad periods, I suddenly won something and I felt great. This year it's been a bit tougher. I think I will learn to have more grit and to find also little successes, not only be happy with the results, but also with the process and everything."

Swiatek will next face either Ashlyn Krueger or Lanlana Tararudee. It would be her first meeting with either player.

Svitolina needs three sets to get past Samsonova

No. 5 seed Svitolina had a tougher passage into the third round against Liudmila Samsonova. Svitolina won the first set 6-2 and took an early break in the second before Samsonova fought back to level the set. Samsonova saved two match points late in the set before claiming it 7-5.

Svitolina regrouped in the decider, winning 6-2 to secure her second victory in as many meetings against Samsonova. She will next face either Katie Volynets or Hanyu Guo.

Seals the deal 💪 Elina Svitolina secures the win over Samsonova 6-2, 5-7, 6-2. #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/qxwUGnb3yx

— wta (@WTA) October 14, 2026

"It was a good match for me," Svitolina said in her on-court interview. "I felt like I was playing good and then she came back in the second set and I had to really step up my game in the third. I'm very happy with the way I could stay mentally tough and continue fighting.

"I think [the key was] a little bit of everything Finding the shots and finding the right ball to attack. I think this was really important and really stay focused and find your way to win."

Both Swiatek and Svitolina are looking for deep runs in Wuhan as they pursue qualification for the season-ending WTA Finals. Svitolina currently sits sixth in the Race to the WTA Finals standings, while Swiatek is 10th.
content.summary: Iga Swiatek defeated Magdalena Frech to record her 40th win of the season and move while Elina Svitolina rallied past Liudmila Samsonova in three sets at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open as both players continued their bids to qualify for the WTA Finals.

content.title: 'It feels like it was a century ago': Sakkari recounts 2017 Wuhan breakthrough
content.description: Nine years ago, Maria Sakkari scored her breakthrough tournament. She still thinks about it to this day, and is on the verge of reaching the quarterfinals again in Wuhan.

content.body:
WUHAN -- Nine years ago, Maria Sakkari arrived in Wuhan as a World No. 80 qualifier and had a breakthrough week, beating Caroline Wozniacki, Elena Vesnina and Alizé Cornet before falling to Caroline Garcia in the semifinals. Now back at the 2026 Dongfeng Voyah Wuhan Open, she still reflects on that run.

"That's when I cracked the top 50 for the first time," Sakkari said Tuesday. "It is a special place in my heart because I had my first big wins against Wozniacki, Vesnina, Cornet back in the day. Some great names that I managed [beat] to back to back.

"It feels like it was a century ago. Sometimes I look in pictures -- nowadays, I feel very young, but back then I was even younger, so I just feel like now I have obviously a lot more experience, more maturity. Back then, I was just a little bit fearless, and I didn't really think about too much. The more you grow up, the more you think about other things. It's been almost 10 years since that run, and I'm still producing some very good tennis."

Sakkari hadn't played singles in Wuhan since 2018, though she did play doubles last year.

Tuesday, she upset No. 8 seed Marta Kostyuk in a 4-6, 6-2, 6-2 comeback win to become the first player to reach the third round. In the first round, she defeated Donna Vekic in straight sets, and Thursday, she'll face wild card Mia Pohankova for a spot in the quarterfinals.

Should Sakkari advance, she'd be into her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes Benz 1000 quarterfinal since Doha in February and her first quarterfinal overall since Athens this summer.

"[Marta's] been playing some amazing tennis this year so I knew coming in I had to produce some very good level," Sakkari said. "Last week against [Elina] Svitolina, I think that I was playing good. I was just not brave enough to take those break points.

"All I'm thinking is I have the chance to try and do something different than last week. The base of my game is there. It's just that [I need to] try to be a little bit more brave in the big moments."

Sakkari said last week in Beijing that she finds the final stretch of tournaments as a good chance to push herself. 

She recognizes that every player has traveled all year, but whoever handles the fatigue the best will be in a strong spot for the beginning of 2027 -- Sakkari was ranked in the mid 50s this time last season, but now sits at No. 35.

content.title: By the numbers: Gauff and Pegula are making WTA Finals history one year at a time
content.description: Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula have been Top 10 fixtures for more than four years, and now they’re headed to a fifth straight WTA Finals. It’s a streak that’s easy to miss, until you look at the numbers.
content.body:
Before the China Open late last month, Coco Gauff told reporters her suitcase was already packed to capacity, and her mother had wondered how the gifts waiting in Beijing would fit. Gauff’s solution was to pack an extra bag, a modest but telling bit of foresight considering that her season, as it has for years, will stretch into the final week of the tour calendar.

On Wednesday, Gauff learned she won't be unpacking for a while. She and fellow American Jessica Pegula each secured a place at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells, a fifth consecutive appearance for both. The season-ending event is familiar territory by now, and each return adds to a number of milestones that are easy to overlook.

Gauff and Pegula have spent years at the top of the sport together, and string of success that is anything but a happy accident. Few players from the same country have shared the Top 10 for this long, and few have matched it with a run of year-end appearances like theirs. Together, they have become one of the most dominant duos from a single country the sport has seen in decades.

Their excellence has become so habitual that you’d be forgiven for overlooking their accomplishments. Showing up atop the rankings week after week and ultimately solidifying a spot in the season-ending field year after year has started to feel like the natural order of things, when in fact the sport has seen very little like it. Here is some statistical perspective: 

Rankings staying power

209 consecutive weeks together in the singles Top 10
Pegula and Gauff have held Top 10 rankings simultaneously for 209 straight weeks. That is more than four years among the sport's leading players, long enough to span multiple seasons without a single weekly update breaking the run.

222 weeks for Pegula, 209 for Gauff
Pegula's individual Top 10 streak stands at 222 consecutive weeks, 13 more than Gauff's. Gauff's entire streak overlaps with their shared run. Pegula reached the Top 10 earlier and has stayed there since.

Four same-country pairs with 200-plus weeks together
Since 1997, only four pairs from the same country have each spent at least 200 consecutive weeks in the Top 10 together:

  • Arantxa Sánchez Vicario and Conchita Martínez: 319 weeks
  • Lindsay Davenport and Venus Williams: 241 weeks
  • Serena and Venus Williams: 224 weeks
  • Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula: 209 weeks

Gauff and Pegula are the first same-country pair to reach 200 weeks since the Williams sisters did it in 2003.

WTA Finals pedigree

Five straight WTA Finals appearances
Both players will make a fifth consecutive appearance, covering 2022 through 2026. They are the first American pair to qualify together for five straight editions since Mary Joe Fernandez and Zina Garrison from 1989 to 1993, and the first same-country pair to match that streak since Frenchwomen Nathalie Tauziat and Sandrine Testud appeared together from 1997 to 2001.

Five Americans with longer individual streaks
Five Americans have strung together more consecutive appearances than Pegula and Gauff's five. Martina Navratilova leads with 17, followed by Garrison with 12, Davenport with nine, Pam Shriver with seven and Chris Evert with six. Navratilova represented Czechoslovakia in her first two appearances.

Both have found success at the Finals, most memorably in 2024, when Gauff beat Zheng Qinwen in the championship match to capture the title. Pegula has had her own deep runs, reaching the final in 2023 and the semifinals in 2025, and now the two return to Indian Wells together once more.

content.title: Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff qualify for WTA Finals in Indian Wells
content.description: Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff punched their tickets to the season-ending event in November, making it five straight appearances for both American stars.
content.body:
• Both players will be appearing at the season-ending event for the fifth consecutive year
  • Gauff is a former WTA Finals champion, lifting the title in 2024
  • Pegula has reached an impressive five finals this season, including two at WTA 1000 level

  • Tickets are available here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden

The WTA announced Wednesday American stars Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff will be competing on tennis' ultimate stage in November as both players have secured qualification for the WTA Finals Indian Wells.

Pegula and Gauff will each make their fifth consecutive appearance at the season-ending tournament. They join PIF WTA World No. 1 Elena Rybakina, Indian Wells and Miami champion Aryna Sabalenka, Roland-Garros winner Mirra Andreeva and Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, with two singles spots still open.

Pegula and Gauff’s qualification means the WTA Finals singles draw will feature multiple American players for the fifth consecutive year.

Pegula is no stranger to the WTA Finals and across her four previous appearances finished as runner-up in 2023 and made the semifinals in 2025.

Her season has been highlighted by reaching an impressive five finals, including two at WTA 1000 level, winning the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships and contesting the title match at the Cincinnati Open.

The Buffalo native also reached the final at three WTA 500 tournaments, winning the Credit One Charleston Open and finishing runner-up at the VANDA Pharmaceuticals Berlin Tennis Open and the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, D.C.

Florida's Coco Gauff has also flourished this season at WTA 1000 events, winning the Cincinnati Open and reaching the final at the Miami Open presented by Itaú and Internazionali BNL d'Italia (Rome).

The former WTA Finals champion, who in 2024 became the first American player to win the title in 10 years, also performed strongly at the Grand Slams to bolster her qualification hopes, reaching the semifinals at Wimbledon and the US Open and the quarterfinals at the Australian Open.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells field includes eight singles players and eight doubles teams from the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard. The top seven in each race qualify automatically. The eighth spot goes to the highest-ranked Grand Slam champion, singles player or doubles team, ranked from No. 8 to No. 20 who has not already qualified.

 This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivalled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment, and culture.

Tickets are available here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

content.title: Guo's Wuhan upset carries deeper meaning; Samsonova, Putintseva win thrillers
content.description: Guo Hanyu's upset in Wuhan over Sorana Cirstea was much more than a tennis match. It was a bright spot in what's been a difficult few months. Plus, Liudmila Samsonova and Yulia Putintseva picked up gritty three-set wins in Wuhan.

related.label: Shi rides qualifying momentum to stunner over Eala in Wuhan
Rankings Watch: Zheng returns to Top 30, Andreeva makes Top 3 debut
How humility and hard truths restored Zheng Qinwen’s fire in Beijing

content.body:
WUHAN -- Day 2 of the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open brought several three-set thrillers, highlighted by Guo Hanyu's 1-6, 7-6(6), 7-5 upset of No. 12 seed Sorana Cirstea in 2 hours and 41 minutes. Guo saved three match points and came back from a set and 4-0 down.

The World No. 240 earned her second WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz 1000 singles win and her first tour-level main-draw victory since Jiujiang in 2025. By ranking, it's the biggest win of her career, and she's the lowest ranked player to defeat a top 20 opponent at the Wuhan Open since the tournament's inception in 2014 -- Cirstea is ranked No. 16.

But Tuesday's win had much more meaning for Guo. Following her first Grand Slam doubles title at Wimbledon this summer with Kristina Mladenovic, she learned that her father became seriously ill and is in the intensive care unit. 

"It's really difficult for me when I come back home," Guo said. "I try to accompany my dad, I try to do something about it. Knowing this actually made me feel quite helpless.

"No matter what kind of efforts you make, for myself I'm kind of struggling recently because mentally, psychologically I always feel something. I cannot just have a happy moment on the court and enjoy the game. I will always have a kind of sorrow, so that's why I made a lot of efforts.

"Today's match in the third set, it was such a thing of another close loss. This kind of close loss is always painful. I always try to tell myself that I try to be myself and leave it to the fate. If God really wants me go for this in my tennis game all I can do is try my 100% on the court and see what is the result."

Absolute scenes in Wuhan 😲 Guo Hanyu with an unbelievable comeback to defeat Cirstea! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/rBBfMq55ud

— wta (@WTA) October 13, 2026

Since Wimbledon, Guo had only played a total of four tournaments in singles and doubles combined. Her personal situation made it difficult to enjoy her success at Wimbledon, and today's win was a bright spot in a difficult period in her life.  

Guo will next face qualifier Katie Volynets, who went toe-to-toe with Australia's Kimberly Birrell. Volynets overcame a dropped first-set tiebreak to defeat Birrell 6-7(1), 7-6(3), 6-3 in 3 hours and 6 minutes. 

Samsonova gets past valiant Siniakova

Liudmila Samsonova started the order of play Tuesday on Center Court against Katerina Siniakova in their fifth overall meeting. Initially, Samsonova seemed like she'd cruise to victory, dropping just one game in the opening set. 

Then, Siniakova, who seemed a bit under the weather stormed back and forced a decider. Samsonova ultimately advanced to the second round, and will next face No. 5 seed Elina Svitolina. She also now holds a slim 3-2 advantage in the head to head. 

"If you give her a little bit of time to play, she plays very, very well," Samsonova said to press. "She has a lot of talent and she can let you play very bad. Today, the goal was not to let her play so much, honestly. So I am so happy about the level that I showed up."

Samsonova said that because she didn't string too many matches consecutive at tournaments in the first half of the year, she feels quite fresh and energetic for the remainder of the Asian Swing. 

Some of her best results have come since the switch back to hard courts, reaching the fourth round in Toronto and the semifinals in Guadalajara. 

"I've had a quiet six months of the year," Samsonova said. "Now I'm starting to actually play better, so for me, I have a little bit more energy because I didn't play so much at the beginning, like not many matches, so at the end, I didn't spend so much energy.

"It's a different end of the season for me because I still have a bit of energy and I will play till the end if my body permits."

Following Wuhan, Samsonova will play in Osaka and is also in the qualifying draw for Tokyo.

Putintseva wins derby with Sonmez

The last time Yulia Putintseva and Zeynep Sonmez played, it was quite the show. 

At the Australian Open in January, Putintseva won 6-3, 6-7(3), 6-3 in 2 hours and 34 minutes over Sonmez, but her biggest opponent turned out to be the crowd. The overwhelming majority of supporters were rooting for Sonmez, and after Putintseva secured victory, she put on a mini dance show. 

Putintseva said that in order to navigate the crowd, she sang a song in her head about rabbits.

The two met for the first time since the Australian Open in Wuhan's first round. Tuesday was a much more mellow crowd, but the drama on the court was still there as Putintseva prevailed 6-7(1), 6-3, 7-5 in 2 hours and 51 minutes thriller. 

The Kazakh will face No. 11 seed Diana Shnaider in the second round Wednesday.

content.title: '150 percent of your focus': Andreeva on what it will take to compete at the WTA Finals
content.description: After a first Grand Slam title and a season full of firsts, Mirra Andreeva looks back on what went wrong last fall and explains why she feels better prepared as she gears up for her first WTA Finals.

related.label: A Slam champ at last! Andreeva overpowers Chwalinska to win Roland Garros
'Girly aura, positive vibes': The many sides of Roland Garros champion Mirra Andreeva
Mirra Andreeva and Linda Noskova secure qualification for WTA Finals Indian Wells

content.body:
BEIJING -- Mirra Andreeva said her 2025 Asian Swing was a "nightmare."

At the time, she was in a prime position to qualify for the 2025 WTA Finals Riyadh, holding onto the eighth spot. However, following a 2-2 record across Beijing, Wuhan and Ningbo, the margin quickly shrunk as Elena Rybakina, who won Ningbo, was now right behind. 

Then came Tokyo, which Andreeva decided not to play. That choice opened the door for Rybakina, who now controlled her own destiny and just need to make the semifinals. The rest is history as Rybakina made the semifinals, and ultimately won her first WTA Finals championships.

"I think we all know that I just messed up big time," Andreeva said to wtatennis.com in Beijing. "Every match that [Rybakina] had to win in order to qualify, she did. Every tournament that she had to play to qualify, she did.

"You learn from your mistakes sometimes, and even though last year was pretty harsh because when I saw that she won -- I think it was quarterfinal match in Tokyo -- I was like, 'Ughh yeah, of course.' I was disappointed."

This year, Andreeva doesn't have to worry about repeating the same mistake. While in Beijing, she qualified for her first-career WTA Finals as one of the elite eight heading to Indian Wells. 

Andreeva, 19, is having a career-best season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, highlighted by her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros, where she won the Coupe Suzanne-Lenglen in Paris. She also captured titles in Adelaide and Linz and reached finals in Madrid and Beijing.

"We did a pretty good job this year focusing on sometimes maybe not playing a certain week, sometimes playing more like we did with a clay season," Andreeva said. "I played [almost] every single tournament that there was on clay. That also brought me a lot of points in order to help me qualify for the finals.

"Having my team that is super experienced around me, kind of giving me advice on how to preserve my energy, how to maybe spend less time on site, how to focus on whatever stuff that I have to focus on in order to play well. I think just a mix of all these aspects just helped me to play consistent and earn enough points to qualify."

With her win in Paris, Andreeva had always been in a strong spot to qualify, but she didn't think about the WTA Finals until Beijing. Throughout the season, she was focusing on building up to the majors, and with those complete, her focus is now on Indian Wells.

After a runner-up finish in Beijing, Andreeva elected to skip Wuhan with a change of schedule. She is next scheduled to return at Indian Wells.

"In the beginning of the year, I don't think about that at all," Andreeva said. "I didn't think about finals. I didn't think if I would have enough points to qualify, if how good I needed to play. As soon as the [Beijing] tournament started, I started to think about that.

"I started to look at different players, how many points they had, how many matches I had to win. So,  doing a little bit of math as well, but then after that, I just tried to focus on playing well. If I focus on that, the points will come and therefore I'll be able to qualify."

Andreeva's 2026 season has been her career-best, earning 50 wins through her 66 matches. Though her 2026 Indian Wells tournament wasn't her best, she'll return to Tennis Paradise, a spot where she won her second WTA 1000 title in 2025. 

While Indian Wells brings an energetic atmosphere in March as a combined tournament, she's excited for the smaller contingent of players and teams, an indication she earned her spot among the season's top players. 

"I've never been there in the fall," Andreeva said. "It's pretty interesting to go there when the official tournament is not on, when there's going to be twice less players, such a big facility, a lot of courts, and it's just going to be for basically 20, 25, 30 people, I guess overall.

"I'm just super excited to come there as well because Indian Wells then is one of my favorite tournaments, ery happy to play on those courts again."

A new challenge that Indian Wells will present Andreeva is she won't work her way through the draw to eventually play top seeded players.

Rather, she'll face the best of the best every match, something she's looking forward to embracing. 

"Every match will have to require like 150% of your focus, of your mental side, of your physical side as well," Andreeva said. "Every match that you're going to have to play is going to be super tough.

"Here, first round 'Bam!' You can play against Aryna or Elena and of course, that's not going to be easy, but I personally worked for that the whole year, so I'm just excited to see what it's going to feel like."

content.description: Shi Han's dream week in Wuhan rolled on Monday as the Chinese qualifier rallied from a set down to upset No. 19 Alexandra Eala 4-6, 6-3, 6-3. The victory marked Shi's first Top 20 win and continued a breakout run that began in qualifying.

'Back to normal': Pegula ready for late-season push in Wuhan

content.body:
After arriving in Wuhan without a Top 100 win to her name, Chinese qualifier Shi Han earned her third in a matter of days Monday night, rallying from a set down to upset No. 19 Alexandra Eala 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 in 2 hours, 27 minutes.

"I'm really excited now because my opponent, their ranking is [No. 19]," Shi told reporters. "I think I played really well today, and we also played a very good match. I'm so happy to win this match."

For Shi, the formula behind the victory was simple.

"I tried to be patient and play my best tennis. I tried my best on the court, and I tried to save every ball."

Winning big in Wuhan 🤩 Shi Han defeats Eala in a three-set battle! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/CJPuZ2zuzL

— wta (@WTA) October 12, 2026

The World No. 217 also came from a set down to defeat Peyton Stearns in the first round of qualifying before toppling the in-form Kamilla Rakhimova in straight sets to reach the main draw on home soil. The breakthrough run comes just two weeks after she pushed eventual champion Zheng Qinwen to three sets in the first round in Beijing.

The win was Shi's third WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz main-draw victory and her first since Hong Kong in 2024. It also marked her first WTA 1000 main-draw win.

How it happened

There was little to separate Shi and Eala through the first 15 games. Eala broke to steal the opening set, reeling off the final five points from 40-0 down, and held a 3-2 lead in the second with momentum seemingly on her side.

From there, however, the match swung decisively toward Shi. She won four straight games to force a third set, then extended the run to seven consecutive games to open a 3-0 lead in the decider. Eala remained steady on serve, but she could not slow Shi's dominance behind her delivery down the stretch.

Over her final four service games, Shi won 16 of 18 points. After Eala held to stay within reach, Shi confidently served out the match to secure the first Top 20 win of her career.

From qualifying to Round 2 🌟 Shi Han fights to a big win against Eala, her first Top 20 victory! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/8R9UeaBtK2

— wta (@WTA) October 12, 2026

Nearly every key statistic favored Shi. She hit more aces (4-0), landed a higher percentage of first serves (64% to 60%), won more first-serve points (78% to 64%), struck more winners (31 to 20), committed fewer unforced errors (33 to 37) and generated more break-point opportunities (9 to 3). She also won 100 total points to Eala's 88.

Get to know Shi

Shi, 21, owns career-high rankings of No. 200 in singles and No. 213 in doubles. She has won seven ITF singles titles, including four this season. In June, she swept the singles and doubles crowns at the W50 Elvas.

She made her WTA Tour debut as a wildcard at the 2024 China Open and earned her first tour-level victory later that year in Guangzhou over Jessika Ponchet.

Her second tour-level win came at her next tournament in Hong Kong and was followed by a nearly two-year drought that ended with Monday's upset of Eala.

Shi will face Leylah Fernandez in the second round after the Canadian defeated Ekaterina Alexandrova in three sets earlier Monday. It will be their first meeting.
